findings.evidence: This recommendation applies to items returned within 60 days of their due date... matching the return-rate pattern the pilot data actually established.
findings.fix: Either show the days-to-return distribution from the pilot that establishes 60 days as the right cutoff, or drop the claim that the cutoff matches an established pattern and justify the 60-day window on its own stated grounds (e.g., operational cost, replacement-billing timelines).
findings.location: Recommendation section, third paragraph (the 60-day return window sentence)
findings.violation: The claim that the 60-day cutoff matches a pattern the pilot data established is offered as evidence-backed, but the earlier pilot description (What the Pilot Showed) reports only a single aggregate on-time-or-eventual return rate (94 percent vs 87 percent) with no breakdown by days-since-due-date, so no such pattern is shown anywhere in the artifact for a reader to check.
